records.title: Sanchi's sculpted gateways
records.dateNote: The source assigns ornamentation to the first century, without an exact year. The 1–100 window means the work may fall within this period; it does not establish that it occurred in 1 CE or in every year shown.
records.summary: Sanchi's four gateways received sculptural ornamentation during the Satavahana period.
records.locationNote: UNESCO's reference point for the Sanchi monument group, not a surveyed location for an individual gateway.

citations.locator: Outstanding Universal Value → Brief synthesis, paragraph on Stupa 1
citations.supports: Gateway ornamentation and first-century dating. Property coordinates supply the site reference point.

records.title: A new chapter at Ajanta
records.dateNote: This broad window follows UNESCO's introductory description. It is not a continuous building schedule or a statement of political control.
records.summary: A later phase added decorated Buddhist caves to Ajanta's earlier cave group.
records.locationNote: UNESCO's reference point for the Ajanta cave group.

citations.supports: The later cave phase and its fifth- to sixth-century date window; site location.

records.title: Learning at Nalanda
records.dateNote: The monastic and scholastic institution is dated by century in the synthesis. These filtering endpoints are not exact foundation or abandonment years. Earlier archaeological remains are a separate claim.
records.summary: Nalanda developed as a monastic institution and a centre of scholarship, with an enduring influence on Buddhist education.
records.locationNote: UNESCO's reference point for the archaeological property; no cultural or political extent is implied.

citations.locator: Outstanding Universal Value → Brief synthesis, first paragraph; property coordinates
citations.supports: Institutional chronology, educational role and site reference point.

records.title: Vijayanagara at Hampi
records.dateNote: 1301 is the start of the source's century-wide window, not a claimed foundation year. 1565 marks the cited destruction of the city, not the end of the dynasty or all successor rule.
records.summary: Hampi preserves the capital city of Vijayanagara, with royal, sacred and urban complexes.
records.locationNote: A capital-site reference point from UNESCO. This marker is not the extent of the Vijayanagara kingdom.

citations.locator: Description; Outstanding Universal Value → Brief synthesis; property coordinates
citations.supports: Capital identity, broad period, destruction year and site location.

records.title: Talikota: the aftermath at Hampi
records.dateNote: The source gives the year. The record concerns the battle's consequences for Hampi, not its exact day or battlefield location.
records.summary: The Battle of Talikota led to extensive destruction at Hampi.
records.locationNote: Marker placed at the affected city of Hampi, not at the battlefield of Talikota. UNESCO supplies the Hampi reference point.

citations.locator: Outstanding Universal Value → Brief synthesis, paragraph on the city's destruction; property coordinates
citations.supports: Battle year and consequences for Hampi; the affected city's location only.

records.title: Building the Taj Mahal
records.dateNote: The detailed UNESCO synthesis gives 1632–1648 for the mausoleum and 1653 for later additions. Its introduction instead starts in 1631. This record follows the synthesis and preserves that discrepancy for review.
records.summary: Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.
records.locationNote: UNESCO's property reference point, rounded to five decimal places.

citations.locator: Outstanding Universal Value → Brief synthesis, first paragraph; compare introductory description
citations.supports: Patron, purpose and construction chronology, with an internal start-year discrepancy; property coordinates provide location.

records.title: Shah Jahan's patronage at Agra
records.dateNote: This is a patronage record tied to construction, not Shah Jahan's lifespan or reign. The same source differs between 1631 and 1632 for the start; the detailed synthesis is used here.
records.summary: The Mughal emperor's architectural patronage is represented here by the Taj Mahal project.
records.locationNote: The commissioned monument's reference point, not the ruler's location, capital boundary or imperial territory.

citations.locator: Outstanding Universal Value → Brief synthesis, first paragraph; property coordinates
citations.supports: Shah Jahan's patronage and its association with the Taj Mahal construction window and site.
